question: How do Dong-A 2010 and Dong-A 2011 selections compare at their respective T+10 fixed-window snapshots?

placement_level_descriptive_difference_2.interpretation: Broad established-role occupancy is nearly identical, while major-role occupancy is substantially higher in the 2011 cohort. Apex occupancy is similar and rare in both.

overlap_and_dependence.window_overlap_calendar: 2020-01-01 through 2021-12-31 lies in both admissible windows
overlap_and_dependence.reason: Thirty-eight people appear in both cohorts and the calendar windows substantially overlap; treating 200 placements as independent observations would overstate independence.

unique_person_first_selection_sensitivit.definition: Deduplicate the two waves to 162 people and anchor each person to T+10 from first selection. All 100 people selected in 2010 use the canonical 2020/T+10 snapshot; only the 62 people newly selected in 2011 contribute the 2021 T+10 snapshot.
unique_person_first_selection_sensitivit.guardrail: This is person-specific T+10 from first selection, not a single-calendar-year cross-section: 2010-first selections center on 2020 and 2011-new selections center on 2021.

interpretive_guardrails: Do not call the 21.7-point Major difference a newspaper/year causal effect.
Selection composition, baseline status, sector mix and list design differ between 2010 and 2011.
The 2010 article has an explicit 2020 prediction label whereas the 2011 article has a generic 10-year-forward framing; the harmonized outcome is fixed-window role occupancy.
Competing events and unresolved/untraceable rows are excluded from primary assessable-denominator rates and remain in original cohort counts.
The first-selection 162-person sensitivity removes duplicate persons but does not make the two calendar target years identical.
headline: At T+10, established-role occupancy was essentially saturated in both Dong-A waves (~97%), but Major-role occupancy was higher in the 2011 cohort (70.0% vs 48.3%); Apex occupancy remained rare (~4-6%).
